evals.prompt: Can you actually try our init wizard and tell me if the prompts make sense? It asks for a project name then an environment.
evals.expected_output: Searches for an existing driver first, then drives the wizard through a real PTY, sends the answers, captures the screen, and reports what it saw with the reproduction command.
expectations: Looks for an MCP terminal server, published skill, or existing CLI before hand-rolling a driver
Drives through a real PTY rather than piping stdin, so prompts actually render
Waits for each prompt pattern rather than sleeping a fixed amount
Reports what was sent, the captured screen, and the finding - not a raw transcript dump
Cleans up any session it created

evals.prompt: The dashboard TUI looks fine for me but a colleague says the table is mangled. Take a look.
evals.expected_output: Reproduces at multiple explicit terminal widths, since layout bugs are width bugs, and reports the width at which it breaks.
expectations: Sets terminal size explicitly rather than inheriting whatever is current
Tries narrow, normal and wide widths to find the breaking point
Captures scrollback as well as the visible pane if content scrolled away
Reports the specific width where rendering breaks

evals.prompt: Our deploy CLI just hangs forever when I run it from a script, but it's fine when I run it by hand.
evals.expected_output: Recognises the TTY difference: the program is likely waiting on a prompt it only renders when stdout is a terminal. Reproduces both ways to confirm.
expectations: Identifies piped-vs-PTY as the probable cause rather than guessing at a deadlock
Reproduces under a real PTY and under a pipe to compare
Explains that programs suppress prompts and colour when not attached to a TTY

evals.prompt: Write me a driver script that sends keys to our TUI and greps the output.
evals.expected_output: Searches for existing tooling before writing anything, names what it found, and only hand-rolls if nothing fits - saying so explicitly.
expectations: Runs a search for MCP servers and published skills covering terminal driving
Names what it found and whether it fits
Only writes a bespoke driver after stating that nothing suitable exists
Does not silently hand-roll because searching felt slow

evals.prompt: Add a regression test suite with assertions for all the TUI keyboard shortcuts and wire it into CI.
evals.expected_output: Out of scope for this skill. Says so plainly - this skill covers exploratory drive-and-observe, not authoring test suites or CI wiring - and points at the framework's own test harness.
expectations: States that building assertion suites and CI wiring is outside this skill's scope
Points toward the framework-native test harness for durable tests
Does not refuse the underlying work, just does not treat it as manual-testing driving

evals.prompt: Run the installer on this box and confirm it completes cleanly.
evals.expected_output: Checks for tmux rather than assuming it, falls back to the zero-install PTY driver when absent, polls for completion output instead of sleeping, and reports evidence.
expectations: Checks whether tmux exists before using it
Falls back to a PTY driver that needs no installation when tmux is missing
Polls for a specific completion string rather than waiting a fixed time
Reports the captured evidence rather than asserting it worked
